units.passage: When convinced that a possible violation was an honest mistake rather than purposeful dishonesty, a faculty member may use the occasion to educate the student about acceptable standards for academic work. In such cases, the faculty member could, for example, require the student to rewrite or correct the original assignment, or to submit a substitute assignment.
units.policy: When convinced that a possible violation was an honest mistake rather than purposeful dishonesty, a faculty member may educate the student, for example by requiring a rewrite or correction or a substitute assignment.
units.why: When a violation looks like 'an honest mistake', a faculty member 'may use the occasion to educate the student' (rewrite, substitute assignment). It is a de-escalation route before sanctions, so P57 (talk and gather context first) is the closest fit; no listed type covers educative remedies exactly. units.passage: No grade penalty; student may resubmit all or a portion of the work
units.why: A flowchart branch for suspected misuse says 'No grade penalty; student may resubmit all or a portion of the work', a lenient teaching-moment outcome nearest to P38. (Reconciled codes: actor=instructor, phase=when-misuse, modality=may, policy_type=P38, unit_stance=neutral.)

units.passage: Inadvertent use should also be reported.
units.why: Asks students to report accidental AI use; it works as a self-report provision (P38), though no reduced consequence is stated, so P38 is the nearest fit.

units.passage: the instructor may request that the student attend a remedial, private session administered by university libraries regarding acceptable ways to document research
units.policy: For less severe cases of plagiarism, the instructor may request that the student attend a remedial, private session administered by university libraries regarding acceptable ways to document research.
units.why: Plagiarism school offers a "remedial, private session" to mitigate sanctions for unintentional plagiarism for students not previously sanctioned; mitigation in return for remediation is closest to P38 (reduced consequences), though it is not a self-report window.

units.passage: Plagiarism school will only be offered to students not previously sanctioned for plagiarism
units.why: Plagiarism school "will only be offered to students not previously sanctioned for plagiarism", limiting the mitigation; the same P38 mechanism with an eligibility condition.
